content_selection.rationale: The selection is strong overall. The brief built a clear lead theme from the Anthropic eval report, the White House SI Force statement and OpenAI's grader incident. It handled follow-ups well, adding only new developments, and it correctly dropped repeats from earlier briefs and marketing press releases. The one clear miss is Satya Nadella's Oct 10 'assume every model is compromised / emergency brake' essay. Bloomberg, TechCrunch, The Verge and others covered it widely, it fits the brief's own agent-containment headline, and it is arguably more important than the Arena or Manus funding items. The WSJ scoop that Meta turned down Amodei's compute request was a smaller miss: it was a Techmeme top story, but leaving it out is defensible. The other exclusions I checked hold up. Apple's iPhone 18 Pro order cuts are mainly a consumer-hardware and demand story with mixed signals, and the Synopsys–China item was exploratory with no named partners.
content_selection.evidence: The brief's own framing is 'Agent containment becomes policy,' yet it excluded 'Satya Nadella: assume every AI model is compromised; build an emergency brake (TechCrunch; explainx).' Bloomberg and TechCrunch both ran that story on Oct 10, and Business Standard noted it came amid the Anthropic/OpenAI disclosures.

selection_disagreements.story: Satya Nadella: assume every AI model is compromised; build an 'emergency brake'
selection_disagreements.rationale: Searches show the essay got wide top-tier coverage on Oct 10 (Bloomberg, TechCrunch, The Verge, Business Standard). Bloomberg framed it as treating powerful models as insider threats and not relying only on model-maker assurances, and outlets tied it directly to the Anthropic/OpenAI incident disclosures and the US disclosure push. A hyperscaler CEO calling for standardized containment and kill switches the day after those disclosures fits the brief's lead theme exactly. It deserved at least a headline, ahead of items like the Arena or Manus raises.

selection_disagreements.story: WSJ: Amodei asked Meta for compute and was turned down
selection_disagreements.rationale: Weaker case than Nadella. The WSJ piece led Techmeme on Oct 9 and was picked up widely (AI Weekly, FourWeekMBA, IT Home). It reports that Meta debated giving Anthropic chips and declined 'for now,' as part of a broader story about executives personally brokering scarce compute. It would have been a useful headline-only item next to the brief's OpenAI/Anthropic run-rate and IPO coverage, though leaving it out is defensible.

factual_accuracy.rationale: I checked the main claims against primary sources: Anthropic's report, Axios's full statement, OpenAI's incident page, Epoch's report, Microsoft's Decision-1 post, Google Cloud's blog, and the arXiv abstract. They match the brief closely, down to specific numbers like 19+1 visa applications, the SI Force co-chairs, $0.042/M pricing, the 35x speed claim versus GPT-6 Sol, the 1.3% flip rate, RHAE 100.0 with 7,518 actions, and SDPO recovery of 35%/15%. Secondary reporting confirms the funding and deal items (OpenAI ~$50B, TypeSafe $870M/$7.5B, Arena $200M/$3.1B, Nvidia–Reflection, Manus $500M+). One sentence goes beyond its source: the claim that OpenAI has extended misalignment monitoring to all RL and evaluation traffic is not on OpenAI's incident page. The page only says monitoring should cover failed and crashed attempts. A few other details I could not confirm (the Stosz quote, the Bloomberg year-end target, Liquid d1 figures, the Senate report, the usage-policy changes). The brief does hedge the vendor figures and the paywalled FT item appropriately.
factual_accuracy.evidence: "OpenAI says it has since extended misalignment monitoring to all RL and evaluation traffic" — the OpenAI incident page only says the incident 'illustrates why monitoring must include failed or crashed attempts.'

length_format.rationale: The structural counts comply: there are 14 Headlines bullets (target 8-15) and 10 deep-dives (target 5-10), spread across all five tiered sections with none left empty. However, every deep-dive far exceeds the stated 3-6 sentence target, typically running 9-15 sentences and appending a 'Why it matters' segment and caveats. The content is dense rather than padded, but this length overshoot is consistent across all ten items, which is a meaningful format violation even though the counts sit at or within the range limits.
length_format.evidence: The Anthropic deep-dive runs about 14 sentences, from 'Anthropic published a report on four kinds of unintended actions...' through 'Transluce's Conrad Stosz argued...'. The Memento 3 and OpenAI grader items are similarly about 10-12 sentences each, against a 3-6 sentence target.

dedup.rationale: Three of today's stories overlap with prior editions: decision models (Oct 7, Oct 9), Reflection AI (Oct 9) and OpenAI's math release (Oct 7, Oct 8). Each is explicitly labelled in both the headline and the section header as a follow-up, and each adds substantive new information: the $870M TypeSafe round and the Microsoft and Liquid launches, the reported Nvidia acquisition talks, and the manuscript withdrawals plus the Lean-formalization gap. The other stories (Anthropic eval containment, the White House SI Force statement, the OpenAI grader incident, the run-rate correction, the Gemini agent, Memento 3, InnovationEval, the usage policy, the Senate report, Manus and Arena) do not appear in the Oct 7–9 editions. No unlabelled or unjustified repeats were found.
